Today’s Sponsor

A Full Year of Seedance 2.5

Every good video takes four or five attempts. Most tools ration your attempts, so people ship the first one and call it done.

Get started on Artlist ➜
 
Breaking News

This Week’s Top AI Developments

📊 Google Read 15 Million Chats

The biggest study yet of real AI use found 86% of it happens outside work, and inside a job AI touches about a fifth of tasks. Under 10% of work interactions automate anything.

♾️ ChatGPT Unlimited for Everyone

Message caps are gone. Now, free users get unlimited text chats and a Think button for harder questions. Paid tiers gain a thinking slider and a Sol willing to push back.

🧠 AI Beats 458 of 526 Human Teams

It worked alone for 16 days on a contest project, then finished ahead of 458 of the 526 human teams entered. The Max tier has never been open before, and the weights land next week.

 
AI Finds

Best of Beyond the Feed

🎓 MIT’s Own AI Syllabus

13 courses walk through AI basics, machine learning, vision, and algorithms, and most of them cost nothing to take.

📓 15 Things NotebookLM Does Well

Every one tried and tested, aimed at anyone who opens the blank notebook and has no idea where to begin.

🎨 41 AI Prompts: Keep Your Face Real

Every one is copy-paste ready, built to restyle your photo completely while leaving your face exactly as it is.

 
Coming in Hot

AI Tools of the Week

  1. 🎬 Movie Maker Studio turns a short description into a finished ad or short film, running in your browser with nothing to install.

  2. 🚀 doany builds your company end to end, shipping the product and site the same day, then getting it found and closing sales while you sleep.

  3. 🏋️ Fit Senpai builds a workout plan around your level, matches it with meals and macro targets, then turns the week's recipes into a grocery list.

  4. 🚀 Leapd turns one sentence into a working business, researching the market, building the product and landing page, then chasing your first customers on its own.

  5. 🎞️ Kinovi generates video from text, images, or a reference clip, and now routes you through a catalog of models including Seedance 2.5.

  6. 🖊️ Ankon AI turns a topic, script, or PDF into a whiteboard explainer, writing the narration and drawing each scene in time with the voiceover.

  7. 💬 Revfer writes your review replies, social posts, and customer answers around the clock, so a one-person shop stays responsive without hiring anyone.

  8. 🧠 BackEngine pulls your scattered company knowledge into one place, so Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini answer with real context instead of guessing.

  9. 🤝 CrafterQ drops a chat agent trained on your own site content onto any page, answering visitor questions and steering them toward a purchase.

  10. 📱 Reelyze breaks your Reels down frame by frame to show the exact second viewers swiped away, and which hooks are landing in your niche.

 

🦾 Launch your AI tool on the #1 AI tools marketplace.

 
Interesting AI

This Week’s Most Interesting AI

Google put Gemma on a Raspberry Pi. Now it translates with the internet switched off.

Speak into the mic. It hears you, works it out, and answers out loud in another language. Every step happens on the board itself. The reply lands before a cloud call would finish connecting. The case came off a 3D printer, the screen is a tiny retro terminal, and the code is public.

Take it underground. Take it on a plane. Take it somewhere with one bar of nothing. It behaves exactly the same, and anyone can build one.

Check it out here ➜

🖥️ Presenton generates editable PowerPoint decks from a prompt or document, running locally on your own models and templates.

🏠 ClaraVerse runs a private AI workspace on your own hardware, with chat, agent crews, and a visual workflow builder.

✂️ AI Youtube Shorts Generator cuts long videos into vertical clips and scores each for viral potential.

 
Prompt of the Week

How to Work With Me

View and copy today’s full prompt

This prompt builds the one page operating manual for working with you, the document almost nobody has written and every colleague, client, or collaborator would use. You finish with a page short enough to read in three minutes, the reciprocal half so it doesn’t land as a list of demands, and the words to say when you hand it over.
